chunks: Seven - Muhammad ibn Ya'qoob, from some of his men, from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' al-Hamdani, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Usayd ibn Tha'laba, from Umm Hani' who said: I met Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir and asked him about this verse.
So I swear by the stars that recede, {15} The ships that run and hide {16}

He said: 'Al-Khunnas' is an Imam who conceals himself in his time when his knowledge is cut off from the people in the year two hundred and sixty, then he appears like a burning meteor in the darkness of the night. If you live to see that, your eye will be delighted.

key_terms.الْخُنَّسُ: The one who recedes or conceals himself
key_terms.انْقِطَاعِ الْعِلْمِ: Cessation/cutting off of knowledge from the people

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Al-Khunnas' in Surah Abasa according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (as) offers a unique exegetical interpretation of 'Al-Khunnas' in Surah Abasa, identifying it not as celestial bodies but as the Imam who conceals his physical presence and public knowledge during the Minor Occultation (260 AH). This interpretation underscores the theological significance of the Imam's hidden state, where his 'receding' from public view is a deliberate divine strategy, culminating in a reappearance as radiant as a meteor that brings spiritual joy to the faithful.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (7) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Sa’d bin Abdullah from Ahmad bin al-Hasan from Umar bin Yazeed from al-Hasan bin Abur-Rabee’ al-Hamadani from Muhammad bin Iss’haq from Ossayd bin Tha’laba that Umm Hani’ had said: Once I met Abu Ja’far bin Muhammad al-Baqir (as) and asked him about (the meaning of) these verses, “But nay!
I swear by the stars that recede, that run their course (and) hide themselves.”

He said: “(The stars) that recede is an imam receding until his news is ignored by people in the year two hundred and sixty then he appears like a burning meteor in the darkness of night. If you live till that time, then your eyes will be delighted!”
